sections.html:
A fast Tyler sale needs three things lined up: a buyer who can close without waiting on a lender, a clear title, and a payoff figure you can trust. A cash purchase tends to hit all three more often than a retail listing does.

Gather the mortgage payoff, your latest Smith County tax statement and any letter about a lien, a code complaint or a missed payment. Those papers show what the closing must pay off and whether a clock is already running.

  • Retail listing: more buyers see it, and you absorb showings, repair requests and a lender's schedule.
  • Private sale: price and terms are yours, along with every form.
  • Cash buyer: fewer contingencies, with an offer that already accounts for repairs.

Tyler is the Smith County seat, ninety-nine miles southeast of Dallas. The townsite dates to 1846 and the city incorporated on January 29, 1850. Older streets near the central square sit beside newer subdivisions farther out, so house ages vary widely. An inspector will focus on whichever systems date a particular house.

Oil, roses, health care and education each shaped the city. Rose growing led to the Texas Rose Festival, held each October. Hospitals, Tyler Junior College, Texas College and the University of Texas at Tyler keep demand tied to local jobs and campuses.

A typical owned Tyler house is valued at $235,300 in the 2020-2024 estimates, with 55.4 percent of units occupied by their owners. Any one house can sit well above or below that point.

The Smith County Appraisal District values property and handles exemptions. The Smith County Tax Office sends the bills and takes payment. The tax office has no role in valuations, and the district is not part of county government, so value questions go to the district at 903-510-8600.

Pay in person, online, by mail to P.O. Box 2011, Tyler, Texas 75710, or in a drop box. The tax office line is 903-590-2920. Card payments add a 2.30 percent fee with a $1.50 minimum, while electronic checks carry no fee. Substations at Noonday and Lindale also take payments. Current-year tax left unpaid after January picks up this schedule of penalty and interest:

  • 7 percent in February, 9 in March, 11 in April, 13 in May and 15 in June.
  • 18 percent in July with a 15 percent collection fee added, then 19 in August and 20 in September.
  • Interest keeps adding one percent a month, and tax unpaid on June 30 goes to the delinquent tax attorney.

sections.h2: Proposed tax rates and the yearly calendar
sections.html:
Smith County runs a Truth in Taxes site for property owners. It shows property values, proposed tax rates, an estimate of the taxes those rates would produce, and the dates and places of public hearings on rates. Budget, revenue and rate calculations for taxing units are posted there too.

Several units tax a Tyler address. The county and the local school district tax every property, and owners may also pay a city and special districts such as a hospital, junior college, water or fire district. Each unit's elected officials adopt rates in August or September.

Between January 1 and April 30 the appraisal district is processing exemption applications and agricultural appraisals. Around May 15 the review board starts hearing protests. If you are selling, the rates set in late summer decide the bill that arrives in October, so ask your title company how the year will be prorated.

Written notice must reach the district within 30 days of the date on the notice of appraised value. If no notice was generated, you can still file a protest by May 20. A letter that names you, identifies the property and shows you disagree is enough, and an online system works with the ID on your notice.

The district's taxpayer liaison officer can explain the process at 903-510-8600. A review board of citizens hears the protest, and you and the district exchange evidence at or before the hearing. Photographs and other records help.

If you lose and appeal, the options include state district court, binding arbitration or the State Office of Administrative Hearings. Weekend or holiday deadlines roll to the next working day, and a late filing is excused only for good cause, such as a medical emergency.

A qualifying homestead's taxable value cannot climb past 110 percent of the prior year's value. No cap exists in the first year an owner qualifies, so a buyer starts uncapped. Owners 65 or older receive a ceiling on school taxes, set at the amount paid in the year they first qualified. The ceiling can rise when they add improvements such as a room, a pool or a garage, and it changes if they move.

State law also gives school districts a $140,000 homestead exemption. Applications are available at the district office, 245 SSE Loop 323 in Tyler, between 8 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, or by calling 903-510-8600.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed or an open estate
sections.html:
Back taxes do not block a sale. The title company pays them from your proceeds at closing and asks the tax office for a payoff good through your closing date. Heirs of an open estate need proper authority first: a personal representative can sign after appointment, or a muniment of title or recorded transfer on death deed may apply.

Bring the death certificate, any will and the latest tax statement to your first call with a title company, and ask what else it needs. Sorting that out early keeps a closing date from sliding once a buyer is under contract.

faqs.q: Which office handles a Tyler valuation complaint?
faqs.a: Call the Smith County Appraisal District at 903-510-8600. The Smith County Tax Office does not handle valuations.

faqs.q: Where can I pay Tyler property tax?
faqs.a: At the Smith County Tax Office in person, online, by mail or in the drop box, and at the Noonday and Lindale substations. Card payments carry a convenience fee, while electronic checks do not.

faqs.q: What happens if Tyler taxes go unpaid after January 31?
faqs.a: Penalty and interest start at 7 percent in February and rise monthly. After June 30, unpaid tax goes to the delinquent tax attorney and a collection fee applies.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to protest a Tyler value?
faqs.a: Thirty days from the date on the notice of appraised value, with a May 20 fallback if no notice was generated. Your own deadline is printed on the notice.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Tyler house while a parent's estate is still open?
faqs.a: Only with proper authority. A personal representative can sign after appointment, or a muniment of title or recorded transfer on death deed may apply. A title company will tell you what it needs.
